Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • The provided RECORD and pre-scan data show no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, install-time setup.py/PEP 517 hooks, or interpreter-startup execution paths.
  • djconnectwise/management/commands/* appear to be Django management commands and require user invocation, so they are not treated as automatic execution evidence.
  • The presence of normal Django application files such as apps.py, models.py, api.py, and sync.py does not by itself establish malicious import-time execution.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • Credential harvesting: no evidence of broad environment-variable collection, .env, SSH keys, cloud credentials, GitHub/PyPI/npm tokens, or similar secret discovery.
  • Exfiltration/staging: the pre-scan zip hits appear to refer to a postal-code field such as company.zip, not archive creation or staging.
  • Network: ConnectWise API/documentation URLs, example.com, and test fixture URLs are present, but there is no evidence tying them to credential theft or C2-style exfiltration.
  • Persistence: no evidence of cron, systemd, launch agents, shell profile modification, or self-reinstall loops.
  • Lateral movement: no evidence of Kubernetes, CI/CD, cloud metadata, Docker socket, or GitHub Actions token abuse.
  • Obfuscation/loader: re.compile hits appear to be ordinary regular-expression usage; no evidence of eval/exec, base64/zlib/marshal staged loaders, or similar malware loader behavior was confirmed.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • The wheel includes many __pycache__/*.pyc files. This can be unnecessary or unexpected in a distribution artifact, but the provided material does not show that they contain a malicious payload or executable logic differing from source.
  • Test assets such as djconnectwise/tests/AnonymousMember.png and test files are included, but there is no evidence that they are hidden payloads.
  • No evidence was provided for sudden dependency insertion, typosquatting, native binaries, or wheel/sdist mismatch.

Additional Verification Needed

  • The provided text corpus is mainly centered on RECORD; full source review and .pyc decompilation were not available in the input.
  • Because many __pycache__/*.pyc files are included, comparing bytecode against the corresponding .py source would be useful.
  • Comparing the wheel against the sdist or GitHub source would help determine whether the published artifact was modified.
